Hi Asha — great questions and thank you for the clear list. Quick post-call recap and next steps from our side: 

1) Summary answer (short):
- Serving layer user data (PII in request payloads and KV caches) can be purged within 24–48 hours after a validated request.
- Audit logs and minimal metadata are retained for operational/debugging for up to 90 days by default; we can discuss reducing retention under contract.
- Backups (snapshots) are on a lifecycle retention schedule; we cannot guarantee immediate purge from immutable backups, but we will mark persisted snapshots for deletion at the earliest backup cycle and provide attestations for application-layer data removal.
- We support both per-user and account-level RTBF. We provide a deletion certificate and summary report when purge steps complete.

2) What I need from you to scope the timeline and formal response:
- Confirm scope: per-user vs. full account?
- Examples of the data types considered PII for you (e.g., name, email, payment token, unstructured text that may contain PII).
- Any regulatory constraints (GDPR vs. CCPA variant) or internal deadlines.

3) Next steps (our internal commitments):
- I'll loop in Rishi (security/infra) for an exact timeline on backups and S3/GCS replica handling.
- We'll deliver a 1-page RTBF workflow + 2–3 bullet SLA options by EOD tomorrow.
- If acceptable, we can add a contract addendum on retention and backup attestation.

Attached: RTBF_process_v1.pdf — high-level workflow.

Would 3pm PT tomorrow for a follow-up call work for you?

Hi all — pulled together the tech confirmation and proposed timeline: 

A) Serving layer purge (PII in request payloads, KV cache, inference traces):
- Standard hosted flow: once we validate the request (identity + authorization), the platform will enqueue a purge job. Application-layer deletion (remove user records from primary indexes, purge KV cache entries, remove ephemeral request payloads) typically completes within 24 hours for accounts under 1M monthly tokens. For larger accounts or accounts with pending long-running jobs it can extend to 48–72 hours.

B) Logs and metadata:
- System access and telemetry logs (timestamps, request IDs, latency metrics) are retained by default for 90 days. We can offer contractual options to retain 30 days or 7 days, but note: full deletion of structured audit trails requires coordination with observability providers — 30-day retention is achievable; 7 days requires additional ops work and a one-time migration for existing customers.
- We can redact request payloads from logs earlier (within 24–48 hours) but the log entries (time/ID) will remain unless a short-retention contract is in place.

C) Backups/snapshots & replicas:
- Backups: immutable snapshots are taken daily and retained per customer lifecycle (default 90 days). Immutable snapshots cannot be mutated; therefore, immediate physical deletion of a restored backup object is not always possible. Our approach: 
   - We will flag the account in backup metadata to prevent any future restores of snapshots containing the account after the RTBF request is accepted.
   - For object stores (S3/GCS) where we have separate object-level storage for account artifacts, we can delete objects on a best-effort basis before scheduled lifecycle expiry if they are not part of immutable snapshot chains — typical time: 7–30 days depending on snapshot chaining.
   - For true immutable backups retained for legal/regulatory reasons, physical deletion may only occur on the backup lifecycle schedule (weeks-months).

D) Derived artifacts (embeddings, indexes):
- Derived vectors and indexes that contain PII-derived embeddings are treated as primary application data. We will run a targeted purge of embedding stores and any search indexes referencing the account; this is included in the 24–48 hour application-layer purge. Re-indexing may take additional background time (up to 72 hours) for very large indexes.

E) Attestation and deliverables:
- We will provide: (1) Deletion certificate (signed) noting application-layer purge completion and scope, (2) Backup attestation describing when snapshots were flagged and the earliest physical deletion window, and (3) A short appendix listing artifacts that may remain in immutable backups with expected retention windows.

F) Proposed SLA options to present to FinTechCo (we can tailor):
- Standard: App-layer purge within 48 hours; logs retained 90 days; backup lifecycle honored (attestation provided).
- Accelerated: App-layer purge within 24 hours; logs retention reduced to 30 days; we attempt object-level deletion within 30 days where possible (requires addendum).
- Extended compliance: App-layer purge within 24 hours; logs 7/30 day options; expedited backup deletion pipeline (requires engineering engagement and lead time).

G) Dependencies / notes:
- Accelerated or expedited backup deletion may require a one-time migration/ops ticket and a short maintenance window.
- Legal may request export of the deletion certificate for audit purposes; we can produce a PDF signed by our security lead.

Action items: Camila — share the SLA options + this tech summary with Asha; if they want Accelerated/Extended, we should schedule a short call with our infra ops to scope runbook and cost impact.

Happy to join the call if needed.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
